$description: The single source of truth for Malachi's interface tokens: color, type, spacing, size, radius, border, shadow, density, motion and easing. Colors are authored in OKLCH. `mix malachi.tokens` generates assets/src/styles/tokens.css, tui/src/theme/generated.rs, lib/malachi/ui/tokens.ex and docs/design/tokens.snapshot.json from it, and `mix malachi.tokens --check` fails the build when any of them drifts. Nothing hand mirrors a value. See docs/design/operator-interfaces.md section 4.

$meta.profile: DTCG-shaped, privately pinned. The DTCG Design Tokens Format Module is a preview draft that states it must not be implemented, so this file follows its shape for interoperability. Its structure and every rule below are validated by Malachi.UI.TokenGen.Source, which is the one place they are defined.
gates: Regenerate and compare: `mix malachi.tokens --check` fails on any generated file that differs from what this file produces.
Raw color literal: the same check fails on any #hex, oklch(, rgb(, rgba(, hsl(, hsla(, Color::Rgb, Color::Indexed or named Color:: in assets/src or tui/src outside the generated files.

Cross language contract: an ExUnit test parses tokens.css, generated.rs and the Elixir module and compares each with tokens.snapshot.json in both directions, so a missing and an extra token each fail. The web and the terminal projects add their own native test when they land (#231, #233).

Contrast and distinguishability: every pair in $contrast in both themes, the deuteranopia distance in $cvd, the distance between colors of different meanings in $apart, the gamut tolerance in $gamut, and distinct terminal colors for every token in $terminal.distinct.

web.$description: CSS custom properties on :root and .dark, exposed through @theme inline.

elixir.$description: Malachi.UI.Tokens, for any server rendered fallback page.

tui.$description: Rust consts. Three tiers per theme: TRUECOLOR, ANSI256, ANSI16. The 256 tier is quantised perceptually at generate time unless $ansi256 declares the index. The 16 tier is hand declared in $ansi16 and is never computed, because a nearest neighbour search collapses state.damaged onto state.fenced. This list and the keys of $ansi16 must name the same tokens.

base.$description: The shadcn semantic set, adopted unchanged. primary is deliberately NOT the brand accent: it is bound to the default button, selected states and badges, and a saturated primary fights the state colors that carry the real meaning.

alias.$description: Semantic aliases the design system's components use. Each one is a reference, so a theme changes them through the token it names.

focus-accent.$description: Decoration beside a focused element, never the only sign of focus; the focus indicator is focus-ring. Not contrast gated for that reason.

brand.$description: Amber, carried over from benchmark/dashboard/index.html so the console is continuous with the one page in this project that was designed on purpose. Never a state. focus-accent carries it as decoration beside a focused element and is never the only sign of focus: ring is the focus indicator and the one the contrast gate holds at 3:1, while the amber reaches only about 2:1 on the light surfaces. The logo keeps its own navy and cyan from docs/logo.svg, which appear in the logo and nowhere else.

logo-tile.$description: The logo's navy tile, #0a0e27. The logo only.

logo-mark.$description: The logo's cyan mark, #00d9ff. The logo only.

state.$description: Malachi's own vocabulary. Capped at what the control plane can actually distinguish. A vocabulary larger than the state machine becomes a lie in the docs and in the translation catalog.

active.$description: Taking writes: an active segment, a serving range, an alive node.

sealed.$description: Sealed and settled. Calm, not celebratory.

fenced.$description: Write fenced. Neither healthy nor broken.

damaged.$description: Rot, torn tail, bad CRC, bad magic.

behind.$description: A copy short of the sealed length, or a consumer behind.

ahead.$description: A copy past the sealed length (#175). Rare and serious, and deliberately not red, so it does not read as ordinary damage.

blocked.$description: A range that cannot take writes (#91).

unknown.$description: The control plane cannot currently answer. Not an error.

severity.$description: Signals roll up through these. The health score arithmetic is published: ok counts 1, warning 0.5, error 0, worst child wins at every level.

chart.$description: Time series only. Never reused for a state or a cluster. Each series reaches 3:1 on the background and on the card ($contrast) and stays apart for a deuteranope ($cvd), which in the light theme is why series 4 and 5 are rust and blue violet rather than two more warm yellows.

cluster.$description: The identity color an operator picks for a cluster, so two consoles open side by side are told apart at a glance. Identity only: never a state, never a time series. The same in both themes, checked for deuteranopia distinguishability among themselves ($cvd) and kept apart from every state color ($apart), which is why there is an orange and no amber: an amber would read as state.fenced. Text on a swatch uses cluster-foreground.

overlay.$description: The scrim behind a dialog or a sheet.

shadow.$description: The colors the shadow tokens are drawn in.

$contrast.$description: Every pair checked in both themes, WCAG 2.2 contrast computed on the sRGB the screen shows after the $gamut clip. A pair names its role and the generator fixes the floor, so no pair can be given a weaker one: text is 4.5 (1.4.3), graphic is 3 (1.4.11): every state, chart series and the control border (input) on background and card, the focus ring on background, card, muted and popover, and sidebar.ring on the sidebar background and accent. A state or chart color drawn on any other surface, or destructive used as text, needs its pair added here first. border is a divider, not a control boundary, and is not gated. A pair whose either side carries alpha is refused rather than composited.

$cvd.$description: Colors that must stay apart for an operator with deuteranopia: the Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes 2009 simulation at severity 1.0, applied in linear sRGB, then the OKLab distance between every two members of a set, per theme.

$apart.$description: Colors with different meanings that must never look alike. Every member of these stays at least minDeltaEOK from every member of from, in OKLab, in each theme. A cluster's identity color must not read as a state.

$gamut.$description: Colors reach the web stylesheet and Malachi.UI.Tokens as authored OKLCH, since both are CSS a browser draws. The terminal palette, the contrast and color vision checks and the snapshot's srgb8 get sRGB, clipped in linear light. A clip that moves a color further than this OKLab distance is an authoring error, so generation fails and names the token.

$ansi16.$description: Hand declared, never computed. A naive nearest neighbour collapses state.damaged and state.fenced onto the same red, which is exactly the distinction an operator needs at 3 a.m. Values are ANSI SGR color numbers; ratatui's named Color variants are emitted for them. The sentinel `default` emits no color and inherits the terminal's own, and is allowed only on a token in $terminal.inherited (operator-interfaces.md section 8.4).

$ansi256.$description: Hand declared exceptions to the perceptual quantisation, per theme. Generation never picks a second choice by itself: when two tokens in $terminal.distinct land on the same index it fails, and the fix is declared here. In the dark theme state.fenced and state.behind both quantise to 214; behind takes 221 (#ffd75f), the nearest index left that stays yellow rather than olive.

$terminal.$description: Terminal only concerns. See operator-interfaces.md section 8.4.
$terminal.$inheritedNote: Inherited tokens emit Color::Reset in every tier of the palette and inherit the terminal's own background and foreground, as k9s does. A TUI that paints its own dark background inside a configured light terminal reads as broken and destroys transparency setups. The theme_background override paints both from the same theme instead: the PAINTED consts carry the theme's background and foreground in truecolor and 256 colors, and painted16 below in 16 colors, so the two never come from different sources.

painted16.$description: The pair theme_background paints in 16 colors. Background and foreground always come from the same row, never one inherited and one painted.

modifiers.$description: Because a 16 color terminal cannot carry eight distinct states by hue alone, and because meaning is never encoded in color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).

glyphs.$description: Colour depth and glyph richness are two orthogonal degradation axes with separate config keys, as btop separates truecolor from graph_symbol. Nerd Font glyphs are opt in, off by default, and versioned, because codepoints moved between Nerd Fonts v2 and v3 and there is no reliable way to detect glyph coverage.

detection.$description: The terminfo.dev order, applied exactly. COLORTERM is the only positive truecolor signal; TERM=xterm-256color means an indexed palette, not 24 bit.
order: OSC probes, parallel, 100 to 200 ms timeout, degrade on no reply

typography.$description: Interface text uses the system stack; every identifier, cursor, key, byte size, hash and duration uses the monospace stack with tabular figures (operator-interfaces.md section 4.4).

density.$description: Row heights. WCAG 2.5.8 sets the floor for a pointer target at 24 by 24 CSS pixels, so the compact tier is only permitted on rows that carry no inline target.

default.$description: The default. Matches Carbon's small row.

compact.$description: Only where there are no inline targets.

height.$description: The row height in force. A .density-<mode> class on an ancestor switches it, so one switch writes one token.

motion.$description: Nothing above 150 ms, and only on a state the operator caused. Data surfaces do not move by default. Explicitly forbidden: full page spinners, number roll ups, slide in on a tail, and shimmer on a refetch.
